post.description: Set up Blowhorn on this computer, safely and repeatably. Each step checks first and changes only what is missing or stale, so running it again is safe; every line says ok (already in place), changed (written by this run), planned, declined, todo (needs you) or failed. It checks that blowhorn is on PATH, lists your Chrome profiles from Chrome's Local State file, writes the Chrome extension's native-messaging host when it is missing or stale, adds the marked PATH block to your shell startup files (~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc, ~/.config/fish/config.fish) when it is missing, so new terminals find blowhorn in ~/.local/bin, and checks your Blowhorn sign-in. Before it writes the native host it says, in plain language, which Chrome profiles the file reaches and asks; the PATH block is asked about the same way; --yes answers yes for a script, and --dry-run writes nothing. With --json, or with no terminal to ask in, nobody is asked: it writes nothing and reports planned. It never starts, opens or attaches to Chrome and installs no extension. It ends with what is left for you: sign in, install the extension from the Chrome Web Store, check it answers, and get the app from blowhorn.ai/download. --json prints the same as one object.

post.description: Send one message to Slack as one profile, or as each of several (--profile a,b: one after another, each with its own idempotency key, ledger entry and result; one profile's failure never stops the next, and exit is 0 only when every profile succeeded), exactly once. A dry run unless --confirm: the dry run resolves the credential, the target and the idempotency key and says what would happen. --target takes a message link (a thread reply: the ?thread_ts= parent when the link is a reply's), a channel link (a top-level post), or #channel, @user or a channel id with --workspace. The text comes from --message, --file <path>, or stdin with --message - or --file -, and is sent untouched (Slack mrkdwn included). Every send carries a client_msg_id and is claimed in the store's send ledger under its idempotency key (--idempotency-key, else derived from profile, workspace, channel, thread and text) before it goes out: a key already sent replays its ts and link without sending again, and a send whose answer was never recorded is 'outcome unknown' and is never resent automatically. The result names the credential that ran (--slack-auth), whether that was a fallback, warns when a token may show a Slack app's attribution, and reports bot_id, app_id, bot_profile or subtype on Slack's answer. Exit codes: 0 sent, replayed or previewed; 1 refused (credential or Slack); 2 usage or key conflict; 3 store unavailable or a contended key; 4 outcome unknown; 5 rate-limited (Retry-After kept).

post.description: Collect people into the store from GitHub or LFX. GitHub lists one audience of one or more repositories (stargazers unless you name another) and stores one row per login. LFX reads one mentorship project's mentee list and upserts the mentees roster. One run names one platform: --repo and --audience belong to GitHub, --project and --start-page belong to LFX. A GitHub run lists the audience with the profile's stored GH_TOKEN. --dry-run lists that audience and writes nothing. Addresses are not printed. An LFX dry run names the list and writes nothing; a real LFX run reads each profile through Chrome. It does not follow, connect, or send mail.

post.description: Stop everything, right now: on this machine, or on every machine sharing the store with --all. A stop does what a pause does -- nothing new is claimed anywhere it covers -- and one thing more: work already running stops at its next safe point, never mid-post, so a pass mid-flight on another machine, or a manual or agent run there, ends the way a cancelled one does and its work returns to the queue. 'blowhorn stop --resume' lifts a stop, and lifts only the pause the stop itself set: a pause that was already in place when the stop landed stays in place.

post.description:
Report whether this computer can use Blowhorn, and say why not when it cannot: signed in, a client the server still accepts, and a member of the organization. --replay-spool also drains the results already waiting in the local write-back spool; apart from it, nothing here writes anything.

Exits 0 when the store is usable and 3 when it is not -- the same code every other command uses for an unreachable store, so a wrapper can tell an outage from a failed job. --json emits the check as one object: ok, exitCode, cause, error, organization, reachable, spoolDepth, warnings, rungs, replay and cloud; configured is always true, and configPath, configMode, dsn, tunnel, serverVersion, schema and validation are always null.

post.description: Remove Blowhorn from this machine: the background service (the ai.blowhorn.service LaunchAgent, booted out and its file removed), the Chrome native host (the com.blowhorn.chrome_extension manifest, its launcher under ~/Library/Application Support/Blowhorn, and the every-profile install entries 'chrome extension-install --all-profiles' wrote), the ~/.local/bin/blowhorn launcher tools/install.sh wrote (a launcher without the installer's marker is kept), the marked PATH block in ~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc and ~/.config/fish/config.fish (only the block comes out; the rest of each file stays), /Applications/Blowhorn.app (the bundle first unregisters its own Login Items entries - open at login and the background service - through its --unregister-login-items; a bundle too old to have it is reported not unregistered, naming System Settings > General > Login Items as the step left to you), and the checkout's venv/ (--venv-dir, else BLOWHORN_VENV_DIR, else <checkout>/venv, removed only when it holds pyvenv.cfg), node_modules/, desktop/node_modules/ and data/logs/. Every item is reported as removed, not present, not checked, kept, not unregistered or failed, in that order; a failed or not-unregistered item is reported and the run goes on, exiting 1 at the end. The sign-in on this machine (the Keychain item, the account record, and the guided setup progress) is removed on every uninstall. Local data is kept and named -- the store connection file an older version wrote (no longer read), the desktop app's state, Blowhorn's own Chrome trees and the checkout's data/cache/ (each profile's runtime state) -- unless --purge is given, which removes it after you type 'purge' at the prompt (or pass --yes, which --json needs); your Blowhorn account is never touched. Nothing under a Chrome profile is read or written: nobody is signed out of Chrome, Google Chrome stays installed, and the extension stays on the Chrome Web Store. Refused by name, in a dry run too, while a scheduler tick, a service pass, an extension run, Blowhorn.app, a desktop app started from this checkout or, with --purge, a Chrome on ~/.blowhorn is running, and while a write-back spool this run removes (under the checkout's data/logs/, or the app's state under --purge) holds run records that have not reached the shared store (run 'blowhorn store --replay-spool' first, or pass --discard-unsynced-runs when the store will never be reachable again); a spool in any other log directory is left in place and named with its count. --dry-run lists every item and removes nothing. ./tools/uninstall.sh at the checkout root runs the same code with the system Python once the venv is gone. --from-trash is the run the app makes on itself after you drag it to the Trash, before the Trash is emptied: purge scope is forced, the bundle is looked for in ~/.Trash as well as /Applications and removing it takes it out of the Trash, and the Login Items entry of a bundle that is already gone is reported instead of failing the run. macOS only; Linux and any other platform are refused by name.

post.description: Carry this Mac's local data from an earlier home into this one. It carries profiles, analytics history, every run-ledger line (duplicates included), the write-back spool, the pause and the settings you changed. The earlier home is left exactly as it was, nothing already in the new home is overwritten, and a file that differs is kept and named in the report. Browser session folders are never carried. The pause is carried first, so a paused Mac is paused in the new home even if a later part fails. Each completed carry is recorded in upgrades.json in the new home, so it runs once; a carry that fails is not recorded and the next run tries again, adding nothing twice. While a scheduled pass is still running from the earlier home the answer is busy and nothing is touched. The earlier home is found from --source, then from the engine record the app wrote before this launch, then from the previous checkout at ~/code/blowhorn. A folder that belongs to another macOS user is never carried, even when named with --source; the report says so and carries nothing. --dry-run -- including one that comes from your settings -- only plans: the answer is planned, nothing is written, and the upgrade is still due. The desktop app runs this itself at launch; you never need a terminal for it.
